facts.text: On this date in 1883, the eruption of Krakatoa was heard in Australia, 3,500 km away — the loudest sound in recorded human history, audible across nearly 1/13th of Earth's surface.
On this date in 1910, Thomas Edison demonstrated the first talking motion picture. Within 20 years, silent film — an entire art form — was commercially extinct.
Mongolia has more horses than people. With 3.5 million residents and roughly 4.3 million horses, it is the only country on Earth where horses still outnumber the human population.
The city of Tokyo governs more people than all of Canada. Its greater metropolitan area holds around 37 million residents — roughly 30% of Japan's entire population in one continuous urban zone.
More people live inside a 40 km radius of Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire country of Australia. Dhaka's density exceeds 44,000 people per square kilometer in its core districts.

On this day in 1998, Russia defaulted on its domestic debt and devalued the ruble, triggering a global crisis that destroyed Long-Term Capital Management — a hedge fund run by two Nobel Prize winners.
On this day in 1907, the Dow closed at 50.7. Adjusted for inflation, that same portfolio would need to hit roughly 1,700 just to break even — the index sits above 40,000.

The Dutch East India Company, history's first publicly traded corporation, was so dominant at its 1637 peak that its inflation-adjusted valuation exceeds the combined worth of Apple, Microsoft, and Saudi Aramco today.
Short sellers collectively made over $300 billion in 2022 — the best year for bearish bets since the 2008 financial crisis, when markets fell harder and faster than almost any model predicted.
The S&P 500 has dropped more than 1% on a single day roughly 5% of all trading days — meaning a "rare" crash happens, statistically, about once every three weeks.
On this date in 1883, Krakatoa's eruption produced a sound heard 5,000 km away in Australia — the loudest noise in recorded human history, loud enough to rupture eardrums 60 km from the source.

Your skeleton is not static. Every decade, your bones completely replace themselves, atom by atom, through a process called remodeling — the skeleton you die with shares almost no original matter with the one you were born with.

On this date in 1962, Mariner 2 became the first spacecraft to successfully fly by another planet. It confirmed Venus is shrouded in crushing 460°C heat — hotter than Mercury, despite being twice as far from the Sun.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere roughly 20 km across. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.

The mantis shrimp sees 16 types of color receptors compared to your three — yet it processes color worse than humans do. It identifies hues not by comparing signals, but by recognizing wavelengths directly, like reading a barcode.
On this day in 1883, Krakatoa's eruption was heard 4,800 km away in Australia — the loudest sound in recorded human history, loud enough to rupture eardrums 60 km from the source.
Oxford University began teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford: founded ~1096. Tenochtitlan: 1325.
On this day in 1859, Edwin Drake struck oil in Pennsylvania — launching an industry that, within 150 years, would alter the planet's atmosphere more than any volcano in human history.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died 30 BC. The pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — 23 years before the first transatlantic telegraph cable worked reliably, and 33 years before the telephone.

Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. It spread because it named something wordless.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a longing for a home that no longer exists, or perhaps never did. Untranslatable into English, it carries grief, nostalgia, and yearning fused into a single breath.

On this day in 1859, Edwin Drake struck oil in Titusville, Pennsylvania — and the word 'petroleum' (Latin: petra, rock + oleum, oil) entered common speech almost overnight, displacing older terms like 'rock grease.'

On this day in 1883, Krakatoa erupted with a sound heard 5,000 km away. The word 'krakatoa' itself has no settled etymology — linguists still disagree whether it meant 'white cockatoo' or was simply a sailor's mishearing.

Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan, n.): a look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. From the southernmost language ever spoken, now nearly extinct, it holds a feeling most languages never bothered to name.

On this day in 2012, the Bitcoin network processed its first provably intentional OP_RETURN transaction, embedding arbitrary data on-chain and permanently splitting opinion on whether blockspace is sacred or just storage.
On this day in 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had been live for exactly three weeks, having already burned over 100,000 ETH — roughly $350M at the time — removing it from circulating supply forever.

Satoshi's genesis block coinbase contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not just a timestamp, but a direct indictment embedded in the protocol's first 50 BTC, unspendable by consensus rule.

The Bitcoin UTXO set has never exceeded 5GB despite encoding every unspent output since 2009 — a full node fits on a $20 SD card, making the 'storage burden' argument against running one largely rhetorical.

Ethereum's longest uncle rate spike hit ~20% during the 2017 ICO boom, meaning roughly one in five valid blocks was orphaned — a direct measure of how close the network came to consensus failure under load.

On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet to ImageNet — the paper that ended a decade of hand-crafted features and launched the deep learning era. The GPU-trained network cut error rates nearly in half.

On Aug 27, 2018, Google Brain published 'Large-Scale Study of Curiosity-Driven Learning,' showing agents trained with zero extrinsic reward could play 54 Atari games purely by predicting their own surprise.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes, spent in a matter of months.
Transformers were not invented to model language. The 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper was written entirely in the context of machine translation, and its authors expected it to stay there.
AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — nearly every known protein in UniProt — in roughly 18 months, a task structural biology had pursued experimentally for 70 years.
